examples.en: I rode a boat on the lake on the weekend.
A small boat slowly crosses the river.
We ate lunch on the boat.
I'd like to rent a boat.
The wind is blowing, so the boat rocks a lot.
Kids love rubber boats.

explain: '배'는 크든 작든 물에 뜨는 탈것 전체를 부르고, '보트'는 놀이나 구조에 쓰는 작은 배에 써요. 큰 배는 '선박'이나 '유람선'이라고 해요. '보트를 타다', '보트를 젓다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: '배' is the general word for any floating vessel, big or small, while '보트' is a small boat for fun or rescue. Large ships are called '선박' or '유람선'. It goes with verbs like '보트를 타다' (ride a boat) and '보트를 젓다' (row a boat).

examples.en: An old tank is on display at the museum.
In the movie, a tank rolled into the village.

examples.ko: 아이가 탱크 장난감을 갖고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: The child wants a toy tank.
The car's fuel tank is almost empty.
There is a water tank on the roof of the house.
The soldiers took a photo next to the tank.

explain: 탱크는 군사용 전차를 말할 때도 쓰고, 물이나 기름을 담는 큰 통을 말할 때도 써요. 통의 뜻일 때는 '물탱크', '연료 탱크'처럼 앞에 무엇이 들어 있는지를 붙여요. 군용 차량을 정식으로는 '전차'라고도 해요.
explain_en: 탱크 means a military tank and also a large container for water or fuel. For the container meaning, the contents go in front: '물탱크', '연료 탱크'. The formal word for the military vehicle is '전차'.

examples.en: It is hard to tell the twins apart.
Can you tell real from fake?
The colors were so similar that I couldn't tell them apart.

examples.ko: 공과 사를 구별하는 사람이 좋은 직원이에요.
examples.en: A person who separates work from private matters is a good employee.
I want to distinguish the pronunciation of the two words.

examples.ko: 아이들은 아직 꿈과 현실을 구별하지 못해요.
examples.en: Children can't yet tell dreams from reality.

explain: 구별하다는 둘 이상이 서로 다르다는 것을 알아보고 나누는 거예요. '구분하다'와 거의 같게 쓰는데, 구분하다는 기준에 따라 나눈다는 느낌이 더 강하고 구별하다는 차이를 알아본다는 느낌이 더 강해요. 보통 'A와 B를 구별하다'로 써요.
explain_en: 구별하다 is to recognize that two or more things differ and tell them apart. It is close to '구분하다', which leans more toward dividing things by a standard, while 구별하다 leans toward noticing the difference. The usual pattern is 'A와 B를 구별하다'.

examples.en: My father fishes at the river every weekend.
I went fishing at the sea yesterday.
Tomorrow I'm going fishing with a friend.

examples.ko: 낚시하는 동안 물고기가 한 마리도 안 잡혔어요.
examples.en: I didn't catch a single fish while fishing.
It's hard to fish when it rains.
I fished at the lake and came back home.

explain: '낚시를 하다'가 한 단어처럼 된 말이에요. '낚시하러 가다'는 낚시 자체가 목적일 때 많이 써요. 물고기를 실제로 '잡다'와는 달라서, 낚시하다고 해도 하나도 못 잡을 수 있어요.
explain_en: This is '낚시를 하다' ('do fishing') turned into one word. '낚시하러 가다' is the common way to say you go out to fish. It differs from '잡다' (to catch): you can 낚시하다 and still catch nothing.

examples.en: That player has a very fast serve.

examples.ko: 서브를 넣을 때 공을 높이 던지세요.
examples.en: Toss the ball high when you serve.
Today I only practiced serving.

examples.ko: 상대 팀의 서브가 계속 네트에 걸렸어요.
examples.en: The other team's serves kept hitting the net.
My weak point is the serve.
The score was decided by a single serve.

explain: 서브는 테니스, 배구, 탁구, 배드민턴에서 공이나 셔틀콕을 처음 쳐 넣는 동작이에요. 보통 '서브를 넣다'라고 말해요. 같은 영어 'serve'에서 왔지만 식당 서빙은 '서빙'이라고 해요.
explain_en: 서브 is the opening shot in tennis, volleyball, table tennis, and badminton. The usual verb is '넣다': '서브를 넣다'. Waiting tables is a different borrowing, '서빙'.

examples.en: Who serves first?
I serve with my left hand.
That player served hard.
Next time I'll serve.
Just toss the ball and serve.
It's fine to serve slowly.

explain: '서브를 넣다'와 같은 동작이고, 말할 때는 '서브를 넣다'를 더 자주 들어요. '서브가 좋다', '서브가 약하다'처럼 명사도 자주 써요. 서브를 받는 쪽은 '리시브하다'나 '받다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is the same action as '서브를 넣다', which you hear more often in speech. The noun is also common, as in '서브가 좋다' (good serve) and '서브가 약하다' (weak serve). The receiving side uses '리시브하다' or '받다'.

examples.en: Don't despair just because you failed the exam.
He fell into despair when he heard the news of the accident.
Despairing alone won't solve the problem.

examples.ko: 절망하는 친구에게 따뜻한 말을 해 줬어요.
examples.en: I said kind words to my friend who was in despair.

examples.ko: 모든 걸 잃고 절망한 사람들이 많았어요.
examples.en: Many people had lost everything and despaired.
There's no need to despair so early.

explain: 절망하다는 희망이 완전히 없다고 느낄 때 써요. 그냥 '실망하다'는 기대와 달라서 마음이 상하는 정도이고, 절망하다는 훨씬 더 깊고 무거운 말이에요. '절망하지 마세요'처럼 위로할 때 자주 써요.
explain_en: 절망하다 is used when you feel there is no hope left at all. '실망하다' is being let down because things didn't match your expectations, while 절망하다 is much deeper and heavier. A common use is comforting someone: '절망하지 마세요'.

en: go on to a higher level of school

examples.en: I'm entering university next year.
My older sister went on to graduate school.
I'm going to enter a school to study art.

examples.ko: 고등학교를 졸업하고 바로 진학하는 학생이 많아요.
examples.en: Many students go straight on to higher education after high school.

examples.ko: 성적이 좋으면 원하는 학교에 진학하기 쉬워요.
examples.en: With good grades, it's easier to get into the school you want.
After entering the school, I lived in a dorm.

explain: 진학하다는 지금 학교를 마치고 더 높은 단계의 학교로 가는 거예요. '입학'은 학교에 들어가는 일 자체이고, 진학은 다음 단계로 올라간다는 점이 달라요. 보통 '대학교에 진학하다'처럼 조사 '에'와 써요.
explain_en: 진학하다 is to finish one school and move up to the next level. Unlike '입학' (entering a school), it stresses stepping up to the next stage. It takes the particle 에: '대학교에 진학하다'.

examples.en: A big tragedy was reported on the news.
Many people were hurt in that tragedy.
The government is investigating the cause of the disaster.

examples.ko: 다시는 이런 참사가 일어나지 않아야 해요.
examples.en: A tragedy like this must never happen again.
People laid flowers at the site of the tragedy.

examples.ko: 그 참사를 잊지 않으려고 기념식을 열어요.
examples.en: They hold a memorial ceremony so that the tragedy is not forgotten.

explain: 참사는 사고나 사건으로 사람이 많이 죽거나 다친 끔찍한 일을 말해요. 뉴스에서는 '대형 참사', '참사 현장'처럼 나오고, 가벼운 사고에는 쓰지 않아요. '일어나다', '막다'와 함께 자주 써요.
explain_en: 참사 refers to a terrible event in which many people are killed or hurt. In the news it appears as '대형 참사' and '참사 현장'. It is not used for minor accidents, and it often goes with '일어나다' and '막다'.

examples.en: I like detective novels.
The detective found the culprit of the case.
My childhood dream was to be a detective.

examples.ko: 만화 속 탐정은 늘 작은 단서를 놓치지 않아요.
examples.en: The detective in the comic never misses a small clue.
The kids are playing detective.

examples.ko: 탐정에게 잃어버린 반려견을 찾아 달라고 했어요.
examples.en: I asked a detective to find my lost dog.

explain: 탐정은 사건이나 사람을 조사하는 직업이에요. 경찰에서 일하는 사람은 '형사'라고 불러서 달라요. 한국 이야기에서는 소설이나 만화 속 인물로 더 자주 보여요.
explain_en: 탐정 is someone who investigates cases or people for a living. A detective working for the police is called '형사', which is different. In Korean, the word shows up most often in novels and comics.

examples.en: That child stands out because of the blonde hair.
My younger sibling dyed their hair blonde.
A blonde-haired actor came onto the stage.
My hair was blonde as a child, but now it's brown.
The doll's blonde hair sparkles in the sunlight.
I was told blonde hair suits me well.

explain: '금발 머리'처럼 '머리'를 붙여 말하기도 해요. 한자로 '금'은 금색, '발'은 머리카락이에요. 염색이나 탈색으로 밝게 한 머리는 '금발로 염색하다', '탈색하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: People also say '금발 머리' with '머리' added. In the Sino-Korean parts, '금' is gold and '발' is hair. Hair lightened by dyeing or bleaching is described with '금발로 염색하다' or '탈색하다'.

examples.en: He is a man of few words and careful.
You have to make big decisions carefully.
She is careful by nature, so she rarely makes mistakes.
Right now you need to be more careful.
He is careful, so his decisions are a bit slow.
I'm sorry I spoke without thinking.

explain: 신중하다는 행동하기 전에 깊이 생각하고 조심하는 모습이에요. '조심하다'는 위험이나 실수를 피하려고 주의하는 것이고, 신중하다는 결정이나 말을 가볍게 하지 않는다는 느낌이 더 강해요. 반대말은 '경솔하다'예요.
explain_en: 신중하다 describes thinking deeply and taking care before acting. '조심하다' is watching out to avoid danger or mistakes, while 신중하다 stresses not deciding or speaking lightly. The opposite is '경솔하다'.

examples.en: My uncle emigrated to Canada.
My family is emigrating to Australia next year.

examples.ko: 이민하는 사람은 먼저 비자를 받아야 해요.
examples.en: People who emigrate must get a visa first.
I haven't chosen the country to emigrate to yet.

examples.ko: 그는 어릴 때 부모님과 이민해서 영어를 잘해요.
examples.en: He emigrated with his parents as a child, so he speaks English well.

examples.ko: 이민하고 나서 처음 몇 달이 가장 힘들었어요.
examples.en: The first few months after emigrating were the hardest.

explain: 말할 때는 '이민 가다'가 훨씬 자연스러워요. '이민하다'는 글이나 설명에서 보이고, '미국으로 이민하다'처럼 '으로/로'와 써요. 일이나 공부 때문에 잠깐 가는 것은 이민이 아니에요. 들어오는 쪽은 '이민 오다'예요.
explain_en: In speech, '이민 가다' sounds much more natural. '이민하다' shows up in writing and explanations, and takes 으로/로, as in '미국으로 이민하다'. Going abroad briefly for work or study is not 이민. Coming in from abroad is '이민 오다'.

examples.en: Many curious animals live in the jungle.
The explorers went into the jungle.
The jungle is hot and humid, so it's hard to walk.
The child likes movies set in the jungle.

examples.ko: 비가 오면 정글의 길이 진흙으로 변해요.
examples.en: When it rains, the jungle paths turn to mud.

examples.ko: 정글에서 길을 잃은 사람을 구조대가 찾았어요.
examples.en: The rescue team found the person who got lost in the jungle.

explain: 정글은 열대 지방의 나무가 빽빽한 숲이에요. 일반적인 숲은 '숲'이나 '산림'이라고 해서 달라요. '콘크리트 정글'처럼 도시를 빗대어 말할 때도 있어요.
explain_en: 정글 is a dense tropical forest. An ordinary forest is '숲' or '산림', so they differ. It can also be used figuratively for a city, as in '콘크리트 정글'.

examples.en: A fire broke out on the mountain and the trees are burning.
The old house burned all night.
The blazing sunset dyed the sea red.
The ashes left after the burning blew away in the wind.

examples.ko: 창고가 불탈 뻔했지만 소방관이 불을 껐어요.
examples.en: The warehouse nearly burned, but the firefighters put out the fire.

examples.ko: 불타면 큰일이니까 난로 옆에 종이를 두지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't leave paper next to the heater; it would be serious if it caught fire.

explain: 불타다는 불이 붙어서 타는 거예요. '타다'만 써도 되지만, 불타다는 불이 크게 일어나 활활 타는 모습이 더 잘 보여요. '불타는 노을'처럼 붉게 빛나는 모습에도 써요.
explain_en: 불타다 is to burn with fire. You can use '타다' alone, but 불타다 paints a vivid picture of a fire blazing. It can also describe things glowing red, like '불타는 노을'.

examples.ko: 이 섬에는 오래된 종족이 살고 있어요.
examples.en: An ancient tribe lives on this island.
That tribe uses its own language.
I watched a documentary about a tribe's way of life.
Each tribe has different traditional clothing.
The song of the forest tribe was beautiful.

examples.ko: 종족을 지키려고 마을 사람들이 힘을 모았어요.
examples.en: The villagers joined forces to protect their people.

explain: 종족은 같은 조상, 말, 풍습을 가진 사람들의 무리예요. 게임이나 판타지에서는 사람, 엘프처럼 나뉜 무리를 종족이라고 불러요. 비슷한 말로 '부족'이 있는데, 부족은 한 지역에서 함께 사는 작은 공동체를 말해요.
explain_en: 종족 is a group of people sharing ancestors, language, and customs. In games and fantasy, groups like humans or elves are also called 종족. A similar word is '부족', which means a small community living together in one area.

examples.en: I shifted the car's gear to third.

examples.ko: 자전거 기어가 고장 나서 수리점에 갔어요.
examples.en: The bicycle gear broke, so I went to the repair shop.
Shift to a lower gear when climbing a hill.

examples.ko: 시계 안에는 작은 기어가 많이 들어 있어요.
examples.en: A watch has many small gears inside.

examples.ko: 운전 연습을 하다가 기어를 잘못 넣었어요.
examples.en: While practicing driving, I put it in the wrong gear.
The gears mesh together and the machine turns.

explain: 기어는 자동차나 자전거에서 속도와 힘을 바꾸는 장치나 바퀴를 말해요. 자동차에서는 '기어를 넣다', '기어를 바꾸다'처럼 말해요. '기어가다'의 '기어'(기다+어)와 글자가 같아서 문장을 보고 구별해요.
explain_en: 기어 is a gear in a car or bicycle, the part that changes speed and force. For cars you say '기어를 넣다' or '기어를 바꾸다'. The verb form '기어' (from 기다, to crawl, as in 기어가다) is written the same, so check the sentence to tell them apart.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 의견이 달라서 자주 대립해요.
examples.en: The two of them often clash because their opinions differ.
The ruling and opposition parties clashed over the bill.
There was a period when I was at odds with my parents.
Let's talk first instead of clashing.
Even though they were at odds, they eventually found a solution.
The two countries have been in opposition for a long time.

explain: 대립하다는 생각이나 입장이 서로 맞서서 부딪치는 거예요. '싸우다'는 말이나 몸으로 실제로 다투는 일이고, 대립하다는 입장이 반대라는 점을 강조해요. '의견이 대립하다'처럼 쓰고, 짝말은 '협력하다'예요.
explain_en: 대립하다 is to stand against each other with opposing views or positions. '싸우다' is an actual quarrel or fight, while 대립하다 stresses that the positions are opposed. It appears in '의견이 대립하다', and its counterpart is '협력하다'.

examples.en: I'm dividing the big room into two.
The company split its business in two.
Three people will split the cost.

examples.ko: 화면을 분할하면 두 가지 앱을 함께 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you split the screen, you can see two apps at once.

examples.ko: 땅을 분할하는 일에는 서류가 많이 필요해요.
examples.en: Dividing land requires a lot of paperwork.
I paid the amount in installments over six months.

explain: 분할하다는 하나로 된 것을 여러 부분으로 나누는 거예요. '나누다'보다 딱딱한 말이라 서류, 뉴스, 설명서에 자주 나와요. 돈을 나눠 내는 것은 '분할 결제', '분할 납부'라고 해요.
explain_en: 분할하다 is to divide something whole into several parts. It is stiffer than '나누다' and appears often in documents, the news, and manuals. Paying in installments is '분할 결제' or '분할 납부'.

examples.en: The company promotes its new product on TV.
They loudly advertised the sale in front of the shop.
There are many ads that promote the good points.

examples.ko: 우리 동네 맛집을 친구들에게 선전하고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm promoting my neighborhood's good restaurant to my friends.
You must not advertise in a way that differs from the facts.
We're looking for a model to promote the new product.

explain: 선전하다는 어떤 물건이나 생각을 사람들이 알도록 널리 알리는 거예요. '광고하다'는 주로 상품을 팔려고 알리는 일이고, 선전하다는 정치나 사상을 알릴 때도 써서 범위가 더 넓어요. 일상에서는 '광고하다'를 더 자주 들을 수 있어요.
explain_en: 선전하다 is to spread the word about something so people know it. '광고하다' is mainly promoting products to sell them, while 선전하다 also covers politics and ideas, so its range is wider. In daily talk you hear '광고하다' more often.

examples.en: The customer complained that the food was late.
The residents protest the construction noise.

examples.ko: 잘못된 판정에 선수들이 항의하는 모습이 보였어요.
examples.en: Players could be seen protesting the wrong call.
I'm thinking of going there and complaining in person.
It seems like protesting won't help.
I was angry and ended up complaining by phone.

explain: 항의하다는 잘못이라고 생각하는 일에 대해 강하게 문제를 제기하는 거예요. '불평하다'는 마음에 안 드는 것을 투덜대는 정도이고, 항의하다는 상대에게 직접 따지는 느낌이 있어요. '~에 항의하다'처럼 이유를 '에'로 말해요.
explain_en: 항의하다 is to strongly raise an objection about something you think is wrong. '불평하다' is grumbling about something you dislike, while 항의하다 means confronting the other party directly. The reason takes 에: '~에 항의하다'.

examples.en: The police blocked the protesters' march.
The defender stops the opposing player's attack.
Everyone worked hard to stop the crime.

examples.ko: 몰래 들어오는 사람을 저지할 수 없었어요.
examples.en: We couldn't stop the person sneaking in.
The residents are blocking the development.
If we keep opposing it to the end, the plan might change.

explain: 저지하다는 어떤 일이 일어나지 못하게 막는 거예요. '막다'보다 격식 있는 말이라 뉴스와 스포츠 해설에 자주 나와요. 사람이나 행동을 막는 데 쓰고, 문이나 길을 물리적으로 닫는 것에는 보통 '막다'를 써요.
explain_en: 저지하다 is to stop something from happening. It is more formal than '막다' and often appears in the news and sports commentary. It is used for stopping people or actions; for physically blocking a door or road, plain '막다' is usual.

examples.ko: 표정만 봐도 기분을 짐작할 수 있어요.
examples.en: I can guess your mood just from your expression.
I can guess why he is angry.
I had a rough guess at the result, but I was wrong.
It's a question that's hard to guess.
I guessed their age and started talking to them.
The exam was easy, just as I had guessed.

explain: 짐작하다는 정확히는 모르지만 상황을 보고 어느 정도 맞을 것 같다고 생각하는 거예요. '추측하다'와 비슷한데, 짐작하다는 사람의 마음이나 상황을 헤아릴 때 잘 써요. '짐작이 가다'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: 짐작하다 is to form a rough idea of something by looking at the situation, without knowing exactly. It is close to '추측하다', but 짐작하다 fits guessing someone's feelings or a situation. The phrase '짐작이 가다' is also used.

examples.en: An expert provides commentary on the game.
The teacher explained the difficult poem in an easy way.
At the museum, I met a guide who explained the paintings.

examples.ko: 뉴스가 끝나고 기자가 사건을 해설할 거예요.
examples.en: After the news, a reporter will give an analysis of the case.
I want to be a soccer commentator, so I'm studying.

examples.ko: 그 만화는 역사를 재미있게 해설해서 인기가 있어요.
examples.en: That comic is popular because it explains history in a fun way.

explain: 해설하다는 뉴스, 경기, 작품 같은 것을 전문 지식으로 풀어서 설명하는 거예요. 일상적인 '설명하다'보다 방송과 전시에서 더 자주 써요. 스포츠 방송에서 말하는 사람은 '해설자', 해설하는 글이나 말은 '해설'이라고 해요.
explain_en: 해설하다 is to explain things like the news, a match, or an artwork using specialist knowledge. Compared with everyday '설명하다', it appears more in broadcasts and exhibitions. A sports commentator is a '해설자', and the commentary itself is '해설'.

examples.en: Take the medicine three times a day.
I take vitamins every morning.
I took cold medicine and now I'm sleepy.

examples.ko: 복용하는 약이 있으면 의사에게 말해 주세요.
examples.en: If you are taking any medicine, tell the doctor.

examples.ko: 밥을 먹고 나서 복용하면 속이 편해요.
examples.en: If you take it after a meal, your stomach feels better.

examples.ko: 아이는 약을 혼자 복용할 수 없어요.
examples.en: A child can't take medicine alone.

explain: 복용하다는 약이나 영양제를 먹는 걸 말해요. 일상에서는 '약을 먹다'라고 하고, 복용하다는 병원, 약국, 약 설명서에서 자주 보여요. 약이 아닌 음식에는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: 복용하다 means to take medicine or supplements. In daily talk people say '약을 먹다'; 복용하다 is what you see at hospitals, pharmacies, and on package inserts. It is not used for ordinary food.

examples.en: I majored in biology at university.
Today in biology class we learned about cells.
Reading a biology book makes me curious about the body.
My younger sibling wants to become a biologist.
The biology exam is tomorrow, so I'm studying all night.

examples.ko: 최근 생물학 연구에서 새로운 발견이 나왔어요.
examples.en: A new discovery came out of recent biology research.

explain: 생물학은 살아 있는 것을 연구하는 학문이에요. 대학교에서는 '생물학과'에서 배워요. 이 분야의 사람은 '생물학자'라고 해요.
explain_en: 생물학 is the science that studies living things. At university it is studied in a '생물학과' (biology department). A person in this field is a '생물학자'.

examples.en: That couple broke up last month.
I'm so sad because I was separated from my family.

examples.ko: 사랑하는 사람과 이별하는 일은 정말 힘들어요.
examples.en: Parting with someone you love is really hard.
I had to say goodbye to my friend at the airport.
We were together for a long time, but we ended up parting.
Tears came when we parted.

explain: 이별하다는 사랑하는 사람이나 가까운 사람과 헤어지는 거예요. 연인이 헤어질 때는 '헤어지다'를 훨씬 자주 쓰고, 이별하다는 노래 가사나 글에서 더 많이 보여요. 가족이나 오랜 인연과 오래 못 만나게 될 때도 써요.
explain_en: 이별하다 is parting from someone you love or are close to. For couples, '헤어지다' is used far more in speech; 이별하다 appears more in song lyrics and writing. It also fits parting from family or a long-standing tie when you won't meet for a long time.

examples.en: A helicopter flew over the mountain.
They moved the injured person to the hospital by helicopter.

examples.ko: 헬기 소리가 너무 커서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: The helicopter noise was so loud that I couldn't sleep.
A fire helicopter is putting out the wildfire.

examples.ko: 아이는 헬기를 타 보고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: The child wants to ride in a helicopter.

examples.ko: 뉴스 헬기에서 도로 상황을 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: The news helicopter showed the road conditions.

explain: 헬기는 '헬리콥터'를 줄인 말이에요. 말할 때와 뉴스에서 모두 자주 써요. 구조, 산불 진화, 군용에 쓰는 헬기 이야기가 많이 나와요.
explain_en: 헬기 is the shortened form of '헬리콥터'. It is common in both speech and the news. It often comes up in stories about rescue, firefighting, and the military.

examples.en: I record my favorite drama.
I recorded the class and watched it again later.
I recorded the game, but there's no sound.
Please be quiet while we're recording.

examples.ko: 방송을 녹화하려면 먼저 저장 공간을 확인하세요.
examples.en: If you want to record a broadcast, check the storage space first.
May I record the presentation?

explain: 녹화하다는 영상을 기록해 두는 거예요. 소리만 기록하는 것은 '녹음하다'예요. '생방송'과 반대로, 미리 녹화한 방송은 '녹화 방송'이라고 해요.
explain_en: 녹화하다 is to record video. Recording sound only is '녹음하다', so keep them apart. In contrast to a '생방송' (live broadcast), a pre-recorded program is a '녹화 방송'.

examples.en: Starlight flashed in the night sky and then disappeared.
Lightning flashed in the distance.
A flickering light showed me the way.
His eyes lit up and then he smiled.
The camera flash flashed, so I closed my eyes.
A good idea flashed into my mind.

explain: 반짝하다는 빛이 잠깐 나타났다 사라지거나 짧게 빛나는 모습이에요. 계속 빛나는 것은 '반짝이다'나 '빛나다'가 더 자연스러워요. '반짝 떠오르다'처럼 생각이 갑자기 떠오를 때도 써요.
explain_en: 반짝하다 describes a light that appears briefly and fades, or flashes for a moment. For continuous shining, '반짝이다' or '빛나다' is more natural. It is also used for an idea that pops up suddenly, as in '반짝 떠오르다'.

examples.en: The app has a bug, so it keeps shutting down.
The developer fixed the bug yesterday.
This game has too many bugs.
If you find a bug, please let us know.
The bug is gone in the new version.
Because of a bug, my score wasn't saved.

explain: 버그는 프로그램이나 게임에서 생기는 오류를 말해요. '버그가 나다', '버그를 고치다'처럼 써요. 벌레라는 뜻의 영어에서 왔지만 한국어에서 벌레를 말할 때는 '벌레'를 써요.
explain_en: 버그 is an error in a program or a game. It is used as '버그가 나다' and '버그를 고치다'. It comes from the English word for an insect, but for real insects Korean uses '벌레'.

examples.en: This bird lives in the forest.
The fish lived in the clean river.
I researched the animals that live in the Arctic.

examples.ko: 그 식물은 습한 곳에 서식하기 때문에 물이 중요해요.
examples.en: That plant grows in damp places, so water is important.

examples.ko: 개발 때문에 동물이 서식할 곳이 줄어들었어요.
examples.en: Because of development, the places where animals can live have shrunk.
Countless living things inhabit the sea.

explain: 서식하다는 동물이나 식물이 어떤 곳에서 살아가는 거예요. 사람이 사는 것에는 쓰지 않고 '살다'나 '거주하다'를 써요. '서식지'는 동물이나 식물이 사는 곳이에요.
explain_en: 서식하다 is for animals or plants living in a certain place. For people, use '살다' or '거주하다' instead. 서식지 is the habitat where such animals or plants live.

examples.en: Why is that person acting like that?
That kind of behavior isn't good.
If he acts like that, his friends will dislike him.
I'm worried because my sibling is like that.
Many people came out even in weather like that.
I've never seen such a big dog.

explain: '이러하다, 그러하다, 저러하다'는 이것, 그것, 저것의 모양이나 상태를 가리키는 말이에요. 저러하다는 멀리 있는 것을 가리키고, 실제 말에서는 '저렇다'나 줄인 형태 '저래요', '저런', '저렇게'를 더 많이 써요. 글에서는 '저러한'도 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: 이러하다, 그러하다, and 저러하다 refer to how something looks or is. 저러하다 points to something far away, and in speech people use the forms '저렇다', '저래요', '저런', and '저렇게' much more. '저러한' appears mostly in writing.

examples.ko: 수업 진도가 너무 빨라서 따라가기 힘들어요.
examples.en: The class is moving so fast that it's hard to keep up.
Today we covered the textbook up to page 50.
Teacher, how far have we gotten?
Because of the exam, we rushed to finish the material.

examples.ko: 저는 혼자 공부해서 진도를 마음대로 정해요.
examples.en: I study alone, so I set my own pace.
I was absent and missed the lesson material.

explain: 진도는 수업이나 공부가 어디까지 나아갔는지를 말해요. '진도를 나가다', '진도가 빠르다/느리다'처럼 써요. 일이 얼마나 되었는지는 '진행 상황'이라고 하고, 진도는 주로 공부나 수업에 써요.
explain_en: 진도 is how far a class or study has progressed. It is used as '진도를 나가다' or '진도가 빠르다/느리다'. How far work has gone is '진행 상황'; 진도 is mainly for study and lessons.

examples.en: Today we study unit 5.
The grammar in this unit is difficult.

examples.ko: 시험 범위에 이 단원도 들어 있어요.
examples.en: This unit is also included in the exam range.
We take a quiz at the end of every unit.
The first unit of the book covers greetings.
The teacher gave homework for each unit.

explain: 단원은 교과서나 수업에서 내용을 주제별로 나눈 한 부분이에요. 소설 같은 책의 한 부분은 보통 '장'이라고 하고, 학교 교과서에서는 '단원'이라고 해요. '1단원', '단원 평가'처럼 써요.
explain_en: 단원 is one section of a textbook or course, divided by topic. A section in a novel-type book is usually called '장', while textbooks use 단원. Examples are '1단원' and '단원 평가'.

examples.en: The rocket goes high into the sky.
They launch a rocket into space tomorrow.
The kids made paper rockets.
I watched the rocket launch on television.
Rocket fuel burns very fast.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 새로운 로켓을 개발하고 있어요.
examples.en: That company is developing a new rocket.

explain: '로켓'은 위성이나 우주선을 우주로 보내는 발사체에 주로 써요. 뉴스에서는 '우주 발사체'라는 말도 같이 써요. '로켓을 발사하다', '로켓이 발사되다'처럼 '발사'와 자주 나와요. 물을 넣어 날리는 '물로켓'이나 '종이 로켓' 같은 장난감도 있어요.
explain_en: '로켓' is mostly used for the launch vehicle that carries satellites and spacecraft into space. News also uses '우주 발사체'. It often comes with '발사', as in '로켓을 발사하다' and '로켓이 발사되다'. There are also toys such as '물로켓' (water rocket) and '종이 로켓'.

examples.en: I changed the bed sheet.
The sheet was dirty, so I put it in the washing machine.
I spread a sheet over the sofa.

examples.ko: 차 시트가 너무 뜨거워서 앉기 힘들어요.
examples.en: The car seat is so hot that it's hard to sit.
I installed a child safety seat.
I peeled one off the sticker sheet and stuck it on.

explain: 시트는 침대에 깔거나 덮는 얇은 천을 말해요. 자동차나 비행기의 앉는 자리인 '좌석'도 시트라고 불러요. 침대 시트는 '이불'과 달리 위에 덮는 두꺼운 것이 아니에요.
explain_en: 시트 is the thin cloth spread over or under a bed. It is also used for the seat of a car or plane, which is also called '좌석'. A bed sheet is not the same as an '이불', which is the thicker cover.

examples.ko: 그 선수가 오늘 안타를 세 개 쳤어요.
examples.en: That player got three hits today.
A hit came in the ninth inning and we scored.

examples.ko: 안타 하나만 치면 이길 수 있어요.
examples.en: If we get just one hit, we can win.
Sadly, we got no hits at all.
That batter gets hits well.

examples.ko: 두 번 연속 안타를 치고 나갔어요.
examples.en: He got on base with two hits in a row.

explain: 야구에서 타자가 공을 쳐서 아웃되지 않고 베이스까지 나가는 일이에요. '안타를 치다', '안타가 나오다'라고 해요. 한 선수가 안타를 세 개 치면 '3안타'처럼 숫자를 앞에 붙여요. 소리가 비슷한 '안타깝다'와는 관계가 없어요.
explain_en: In baseball, a batter hits the ball and reaches base without being put out. You say '안타를 치다' or '안타가 나오다'. A player with three hits is described as '3안타', with the number in front. The similar-sounding '안타깝다' (to feel sorry) is unrelated.

examples.en: The soldiers kept advancing forward.
The car parked by repeatedly moving forward and backward.
Even a small step forward matters.

examples.ko: 팀은 결승 진출로 한 걸음 전진했어요.
examples.en: The team took a step forward by reaching the final.
The robot moves when you press the forward button.
The teacher told us not to stop moving forward.

explain: 전진은 앞으로 나아가는 것이에요. 반대말은 '후진'이고, 자동차 기어에서도 '전진'과 '후진'으로 나눠요. 일이 앞으로 발전할 때도 비유로 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: 전진 is moving forward. The opposite is '후진', and car gears are also split into 전진 and 후진. It can also be used figuratively for making progress.

examples.en: The army advances slowly.
The ship moved forward carefully through the fog.
Don't be afraid of moving forward.
You'll be able to move ahead as planned.

examples.ko: 포기하지 않고 계속 전진하면 길이 보여요.
examples.en: If you keep moving forward without giving up, the path will appear.
The robot is moving forward one step at a time.

explain: 전진하다는 앞으로 나아가는 거예요. 반대말은 '후진하다'예요. 사람이나 탈것이 앞으로 가는 것뿐 아니라 일이나 목표를 향해 나아가는 것에도 써요.
explain_en: 전진하다 is to move forward. Its opposite is '후진하다'. It covers people or vehicles going ahead, and also making headway toward a goal.

examples.en: This file is made up of text only.
I copied the text and pasted it into Notepad.

examples.ko: 사진 속 텍스트를 읽을 수 있어요?
examples.en: Can you read the text in the photo?

examples.ko: 텍스트가 너무 작아서 글자 크기를 키웠어요.
examples.en: The text was too small, so I enlarged the font size.
In class we read an English text together.
I sent the meeting time in a text message.

explain: 텍스트는 사진이나 소리가 아닌 글자로 된 내용을 말해요. 컴퓨터에서는 '텍스트 파일', '텍스트 입력'처럼 쓰고, 수업에서는 읽고 공부하는 글 자료를 텍스트라고도 해요. 일상에서는 '글'이나 '문자'를 더 자주 써요.
explain_en: 텍스트 is content made of written characters rather than images or sound. On computers it appears in '텍스트 파일' and '텍스트 입력', and in class it can mean a written passage you study. In daily talk, '글' or '문자' is more common.

examples.en: The new computer has a very fast processor.
The processor is hot, so the fan keeps spinning.
I compared the processors of phones.
The better the processor performance, the smoother the game.

examples.ko: 이 노트북은 프로세서를 바꿀 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't swap the processor in this laptop.
The company announced a new processor this year.

explain: 프로세서는 컴퓨터나 휴대폰 안에서 계산과 명령을 처리하는 부품이에요. 보통 'CPU'라고도 하는데, 프로세서는 더 넓게 쓰여서 그래픽 처리 같은 다른 처리 장치도 포함할 수 있어요. 일상에서는 '칩'이라고 줄여서 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: A 프로세서 is the part inside a computer or phone that handles calculations and commands. It is often called a 'CPU', but 프로세서 is the broader term and can include other processing units such as graphics. In casual talk people sometimes just say '칩'.

examples.en: I resolved to see it through to the end.
I'm prepared for hard times ahead.
I went into the exam hall with a resolved mind.
It's fine to take on a challenge even braced for failure.
This time I practiced with the resolve to win.
I started working, bracing for overtime.

explain: 각오하다는 어려운 일이나 나쁜 결과가 있어도 받아들이고 해내겠다고 마음을 정하는 거예요. '결심하다'는 하기로 마음먹는 것이고, 각오하다는 힘든 일을 견딜 마음까지 포함해요. '각오를 하다', '각오가 되어 있다'처럼도 써요.
explain_en: 각오하다 is to make up your mind to accept something hard or a bad outcome and see it through. '결심하다' is deciding to do something, while 각오하다 also includes being ready to endure the difficulty. It also appears as '각오를 하다' and '각오가 되어 있다'.

examples.en: My mother interferes too much in my affairs.
Don't meddle in other people's private lives.
My boss interfered even in small things.
I get stressed because of a friend who meddles.

examples.ko: 아이를 믿고 너무 간섭하기보다 지켜보기로 했어요.
examples.en: I decided to trust my child and watch rather than interfere too much.

examples.ko: 한 나라가 다른 나라의 일에 간섭하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: One country must not interfere in another country's affairs.

explain: 간섭하다는 남의 일에 필요 이상으로 끼어들어 이래라저래라 하는 거예요. '도와주다'와 달리 듣는 사람이 불편하다고 느끼는 뜻이 들어 있어요. '~에 간섭하다'처럼 '에'와 써요.
explain_en: 간섭하다 is to step into someone else's business more than needed and tell them what to do. Unlike '도와주다' (to help), it carries a sense that the other person finds it unwelcome. It takes 에: '~에 간섭하다'.
